full_judgment: 2. In the writ petition and a supplementary affidavit, the petitioners claim that petitioner No.2 is the owner of the disputed land and the structures thereon which are being used as a religious institution called Dewan Bag Sharif and petitioner No. 1 is the Secretary General of the institution. Petitioner No. 2 acquired 28 khatas or 40 decimals of land in SA plot No. 622 of the aforesaid mouja by virtue of seven registered transfer deeds (Annexure-D to D-6) executed by the respective owners including one Md Jalaluddin at different dates within the period from 27-1-1987 to 12-4-1999. After acquisition of the land petitioner No. 2 developed it by earth filling, constructed mosque and other structures thereon and have been in possession of the property and using it for religious purposes. In respect of the land transferred by the six out of the said seven deeds, petitioner No.2 got his name recorded in the mutation khatian and paid rent (Annexure D-7). The mutation in respect o the land purchased by the other deed is under process. Previously the land of SA plot No. 622 was part of the CS plot No. 777/795 measuring 2.30 acres out of which 75.50 decimals was acquired by the Government and the un-acquired part was duly recorded in different holdings of SA khatian No. 345/2 and the land of plot No.622 remained non-acquired. In 1993, the said Md Jalaluddin, one of the transferors of petitioner No. 2, applied to the ADC (Rev) Dhaka for demarcation of his portion of land in plot No. 622. So Demarcation Case No. 9 of 1993 was initiated, survey was conducted and the revenue authority found Jalaluddin in possession of plot No. 622 (Annexure -11). But at the instance of some vested interest group RAJUK issued a notice dated 11-12-2003 directing the petitioners to vacate the land and the structures of the Darbar Sharif. So, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 7453 of 2003 and obtained a Rule and a stay order. After contested hearing the Rule was made absolute by a Division Bench of this Court in terms of the judgment dated 22-8-2004 (Annexure-C). But sensing their defeat in the said writ petition the respondents signed the impugned notice on 21-8-2004, kept it ready and on 22-8-04 issued the same just after the delivery of the said judgment only to fruatrate the decision of this Court. The petitioners claim that before issuance of the impugned notice, no show cause notice was served upon them and that such notice is a malice in law and infringes their fundamental right guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution to enjoy their property.
